minutes.headline: Planning Board continued two hearings and the 240 Summer St decisions to Aug 26, and issued a storm water completion certificate.
minutes.summary: A new chair ran her first meeting. Two public hearings and two decisions were continued to August 26 because of voting-member eligibility. The board moved a certificate of completion for storm water at one building on a commercial site. It also discussed notification procedures after the 20 Kilburn right-of-first-refusal, heard a legal advisory on the state accessory dwelling unit law, approved minutes, and talked about interim planning staff support.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued two public hearings, 255 Sunny Hill and 3 Lancaster Avenue, to August 26 by voice vote.
The board also continued the site plan approval and storm water permit decisions for 240 Summer Street to August 26 by voice vote.
A motion to issue a certificate of completion for storm water improvements at 1295 Mass Ave was moved and seconded, but the outcome is not audible in the recording.
The board agreed to list abutting community notices as a standing agenda item, after discussing notification procedures following the 20 Kilburn right of first refusal.
The chair will email all five members to confirm attendance for August 26 before the agenda is set; the water supply protection district item may move to September 9.

why_it_matters: Three projects that need Planning Board approval, the two hearings and the 240 Summer Street permit decisions, are on hold until August 26, so neighbors and applicants must wait for that meeting.
The standing notice item on abutting communities touches how neighboring towns learn about land-use changes near the border, including when Chapter 61 land comes up for sale.
